- entire-engineering:design:design-implementation-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to verify that a UI implementation matches its Figma design specifications. This agent should be called after code has been written to implement a design, particularly after HTML/CSS/React components have been created or modified. The agent will visually compare the live implementation against the Figma design and provide detailed feedback on discrepancies.

Examples:
- <example>
  Context: The user has just implemented a new component based on a Figma design.
  user: "I've finished implementing the hero section based on the Figma design"
  assistant: "I'll review how well your implementation matches the Figma design."
  <commentary>
  Since UI implementation has been completed, use the design-implementation-reviewer agent to compare the live version with Figma.
  </commentary>
  </example>
- <example>

  user: "Update the button styles to match the new design system"
  assistant: "I've updated the button styles. Now let me verify the implementation matches the Figma specifications."
  <commentary>

  </commentary>
  </example> (Tools: All tools)

Perfect when colors feel wrong, layouts aren't balanced, or the overall aesthetic needs work that single changes can't achieve. <example>Context: User asks to change button color but result still looks off. user: "Change the button to blue" assistant: [makes change, takes screenshot] "The button is now blue, but I notice the overall color balance still feels off. Would you like me to use the design-iterator agent with 5 iterations to systematically improve the color harmony and visual balance?" <commentary>PROACTIVE USE: After a simple change doesn't fully resolve the design issue, suggest the design-iterator to do deeper work.</commentary></example> <example>Context: User's design request leads to something that doesn't look right. user: "Make the hero section more modern" assistant: [makes initial changes] "I've added some modern elements, but the result isn't quite coming together. This looks like it needs iterative refinement. ## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

32	func (a *PiAgent) HookNames() []string {

41	// GetSupportedHooks maps Pi's native events to normalised lifecycle types.
42	//
43	//   - session_start       → SessionStart
44	//   - before_agent_start  → TurnStart
45	//   - agent_end           → TurnEnd
46	//   - session_shutdown    → (cleanup-only, no lifecycle event — see ParseHookEvent)
47	func (a *PiAgent) GetSupportedHooks() []agent.HookType {
48		return []agent.HookType{
49			agent.HookSessionStart,
50			agent.HookUserPromptSubmit,
51			agent.HookStop,
52		}
53	}

55	// Compile-time assertion that Pi can inject context into the model.

58	// InjectionEvent reports that Pi injects model context at TurnStart
59	// (before_agent_start) — the only Pi event where the embedded extension can
60	// return a message that Pi stores in the session and sends to the LLM.
61	func (a *PiAgent) InjectionEvent() agent.EventType { return agent.TurnStart }
62	
63	// RenderContextInjection emits a {"inject_context":"..."} envelope on stdout.
64	// The embedded extension (entire_extension.ts) reads it from the
65	// before_agent_start hook's stdout and returns it to Pi as a hidden persistent
66	// message. An empty Text renders nothing.
67	func (a *PiAgent) RenderContextInjection(inj agent.ContextInjection) ([]byte, error) {
68		if strings.TrimSpace(inj.Text) == "" {
69			return nil, nil
70		}
71		b, err := json.Marshal(struct {
72			InjectContext string `json:"inject_context"`
73		}{InjectContext: inj.Text})
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, fmt.Errorf("marshal pi context injection: %w", err)
76		}
77		return append(b, '\n'), nil
78	}

97	// piSkillEvents converts the Pi extension's live skill-invocation reports into
98	// agent.SkillEvents. This is Pi's only skill-capture path. PiAgent intentionally
99	// does NOT implement agent.SkillEventExtractor: a transcript extractor would
100	// double-count these live events at condensation (see
101	// TestPiAgent_UsesLiveSkillCaptureNotTranscriptExtraction).
102	func piSkillEvents(in []piSkillEventInput) []agent.SkillEvent {
103		if len(in) == 0 {
104			return nil
105		}
106		out := make([]agent.SkillEvent, 0, len(in))
107		for i, ev := range in {
108			skillName := strings.TrimSpace(ev.SkillName)
109			if skillName == "" {
110				continue
111			}
112			invocation := strings.TrimSpace(ev.Invocation)
113			if invocation == "" {
114				invocation = "/skill:" + skillName
115			}
116			id := ""
117			if ev.Timestamp != "" {
118				id = fmt.Sprintf("pi-skill-%s-%s-%d", skillName, ev.Timestamp, i)
119			}
120			out = append(out, agent.SkillEvent{
121				ID:        id,
122				EventType: agent.SkillEventTypePromptInvocation,
123				Skill: agent.SkillEventSkill{
124					Name: skillName,
125				},
126				Source: agent.SkillEventSource{
127					Agent:      string(agent.AgentNamePi),
128					Signal:     agent.SkillSignalPiInputSlashCommand,
129					Confidence: agent.SkillConfidenceExplicit,
130				},
131				Timestamp: ev.Timestamp,
132				Native: map[string]string{
133					"command": invocation,
134				},
135				Collapse: agent.SkillEventCollapse{
136					Target:           agent.SkillCollapseTargetUserMessage,
137					Label:            invocation,
138					DefaultCollapsed: true,
139				},
140			})
141		}
142		return out
143	}

147	func (a *PiAgent) ParseHookEvent(ctx context.Context, hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*agent.Event, error) {
148		// Stream one JSON value rather than io.ReadAll so the hook never blocks
149		// waiting for stdin EOF that some agents don't send on Windows (issue #1398).
150		parsed, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[piHookPayload](stdin)

153		}
154		payload := *parsed

156		sessionID := payload.SessionID

159		}
160	
161		now := time.Now()
162	
163		switch hookName {
164		case HookNameSessionStart:
165			cacheSessionID(ctx, sessionID)
166			return &agent.Event{
167				Type:      agent.SessionStart,
168				SessionID: sessionID,
169				Timestamp: now,
170			}, nil
171	
172		case HookNameBeforeAgentStart:
173			// Pi emits before_agent_start with a fully-populated session ID, but
174			// we cache it anyway to support the agent_end fallback below.
175			if sessionID == "" {
176				sessionID = readCachedSessionID(ctx)
177			} else {
178				cacheSessionID(ctx, sessionID)
179			}
180			// Provide the live Pi session file as SessionRef so state.TranscriptPath
181			// is populated before any mid-turn commits. Without this, the
182			// post-commit hook cannot condense when no shadow branch exists yet.
183			return &agent.Event{
184				Type:        agent.TurnStart,
185				SessionID:   sessionID,
186				SessionRef:  payload.SessionFile,
187				Prompt:      payload.Prompt,
188				Timestamp:   now,
189				SkillEvents: piSkillEvents(payload.SkillEvents),
190			}, nil
191	
192		case HookNameAgentEnd:

194				sessionID = readCachedSessionID(ctx)

docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:48:When multiple sessions are ACTIVE in the same directory and one session's agent (or subagent) makes a commit, **all** ACTIVE sessions are condensed — including sessions that didn't contribute to the commit. This can produce checkpoint entries with minimal content (e.g., just the initial prompt) linked to a commit the session didn't work on.
docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:50:**Why:** PostCommit sets `hasNew=true` for all ACTIVE sessions. We cannot re-validate via transcript analysis because subagent file modifications live in a separate transcript from the main agent's. Attempting to re-validate causes subagent commits to skip condensation entirely (data loss), which is worse than a spurious empty checkpoint.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:11:Entire also creates temporary local branches (e.g., `entire/<short-hash>`) as working storage during a session. Metadata written to these shadow branches — transcripts, prompts, incremental checkpoint data, subagent transcripts — goes through the same redaction pipeline as `entire/checkpoints/v1`. **Code-file snapshots, however, are written as raw blobs of your working tree without redaction**, so any hardcoded secrets in your source code would appear unredacted on the shadow branch. Gitignored files (e.g., `.env`) are filtered out of these snapshots as a partial defense. Shadow branches are **not** pushed by Entire; do not push them manually, because unredacted source content would be visible on the remote. They are cleaned up when session data is condensed into `entire/checkpoints/v1` at commit time.

docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:48:When multiple sessions are ACTIVE in the same directory and one session's agent (or subagent) makes a commit, **all** ACTIVE sessions are condensed — including sessions that didn't contribute to the commit. This can produce checkpoint entries with minimal content (e.g., just the initial prompt) linked to a commit the session didn't work on.
docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:50:**Why:** PostCommit sets `hasNew=true` for all ACTIVE sessions. We cannot re-validate via transcript analysis because subagent file modifications live in a separate transcript from the main agent's. Attempting to re-validate causes subagent commits to skip condensation entirely (data loss), which is worse than a spurious empty checkpoint.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:11:Entire also creates temporary local branches (e.g., `entire/<short-hash>`) as working storage during a session. Metadata written to these shadow branches — transcripts, prompts, incremental checkpoint data, subagent transcripts — goes through the same redaction pipeline as `entire/checkpoints/v1`. **Code-file snapshots, however, are written as raw blobs of your working tree without redaction**, so any hardcoded secrets in your source code would appear unredacted on the shadow branch. Gitignored files (e.g., `.env`) are filtered out of these snapshots as a partial defense. Shadow branches are **not** pushed by Entire; do not push them manually, because unredacted source content would be visible on the remote. They are cleaned up when session data is condensed into `entire/checkpoints/v1` at commit time.

56	// Checkpoints are stored at sharded paths: <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/

59	//   - For incremental checkpoints: checkpoints/NNN-<tool-use-id>.json
60	//   - For final checkpoints: checkpoint.json and agent-<agent-id>.jsonl
61	func (s *GitStore) writeSession(ctx context.Context, opts WriteOptions) error {

63		// canceled ctx means stop doing work, and creating a checkpoint is the most
64		// expensive write there is. Nothing below here observes cancellation

66		// without this a bulk writer that ignores cancellation keeps minting
67		// checkpoints after Ctrl-C.

77		}

80		}
81		if err := validation.ValidateAgentID(opts.AgentID); err != nil {
82			return fmt.Errorf("invalid checkpoint options: %w", err)
83		}

85		// Ensure sessions branch exists
86		if err := s.ensureSessionsBranch(ctx); err != nil {

88		}
89	
90		// Get branch ref and root tree hash (O(1), no flatten)
91		parentHash, rootTreeHash, err := s.getSessionsBranchRef()
92		if err != nil {
93			return err
94		}
95	
96		// Build the new checkpoint subtree from its current state on the v1 branch,
97		// then splice it back at the shard path. basePath keeps the v1 sharded layout
98		// so stored session-file pointers stay /<shard>/<id>/<n>/... as before.
99		existing, err := s.subtreeObjAt(rootTreeHash, opts.CheckpointID.Path())
100		if err != nil {
101			return err
102		}
103		checkpointSubtree, taskMetadataPath, err := s.applySessionWrite(ctx, opts, existing, opts.CheckpointID.Path()+"/")
104		if err != nil {
105			return err
106		}
107	
108		newTreeHash, err := s.spliceCheckpointSubtree(rootTreeHash, opts.CheckpointID, checkpointSubtree)
109		if err != nil {
110			return err
111		}
112		newTreeHash, err = s.maybeMergeVercelConfig(ctx, newTreeHash)
113		if err != nil {
114			return err
115		}
116	
117		commitMsg := s.buildCommitMessage(opts, taskMetadataPath)
118		newCommitHash, err := CreateCommit(ctx, s.repo, newTreeHash, parentHash, commitMsg, opts.AuthorName, opts.AuthorEmail)
119		if err != nil {
120			return err
121		}
122	
123		return s.setPrimaryRef(newCommitHash)
124	}

- Use read-modify-write on entire `hooks.json` file
- Preserve unknown keys in the `hooks` object (future event types)
- The `hooks.json` is separate from `config.toml` — safe to create/modify independently

## CLI Flags

- Non-interactive prompt: `codex exec "<prompt>"` or `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox "<prompt>"`
- Interactive mode: `codex` or `codex "<prompt>"` (starts TUI)
- Resume session: `codex resume <session-id>` or `codex resume --last`
- Model override: `-m <model>` or `--model <model>`
- Full-auto mode: `codex exec --full-auto "<prompt>"` (workspace-write sandbox + auto-approve)
- JSONL output: `codex exec --json "<prompt>"` (events to stdout)
- Relevant env vars: `CODEX_HOME` (config dir override), `OPENAI_API_KEY` (API auth)

## Gaps & Limitations

- **Hooks require feature flag:** The `codex_hooks` feature is `default_enabled: false` (stage: UnderDevelopment). It must be enabled via `--enable codex_hooks` CLI flag, or `features.codex_hooks = true` in `config.toml`, or `-c features.codex_hooks=true`. Without this, hooks.json is ignored entirely.
- **No SessionEnd hook:** Codex does not fire a hook when a session is completely terminated. The `Stop` hook fires at end-of-turn, not end-of-session. This is similar to some other agents — the framework handles this gracefully.
- **PreToolUse is shell-only:** Currently only fires for `Bash` tool (direct shell execution). MCP tools, stdin streaming, and other tool types are not yet hooked. PostToolUse is in review.
- **Transcript may be null:** In `--ephemeral` mode, `transcript_path` is null. The integration should handle this gracefully.
- **No subagent hooks:** No PreTask/PostTask equivalent for subagent spawning.
- **Hook response protocol differs from Claude Code:** Codex uses `systemMessage` (same field name) but also supports `hookSpecificOutput` with `additionalContext` for injecting context into the model. For Entire's purposes, `systemMessage` is sufficient.

## Captured Payloads

- JSON schemas at `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/` in the Codex repository
- Hook config structure at `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/config.rs` in the Codex repository

## Review integration (`entire review`)

Codex review runs via `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --json [-m <model>] [-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>] -` (prompt on stdin). **`codex exec` fires no lifecycle hooks**, which shapes the whole integration (see CLAUDE.md → `entire review` → "Codex specifics"):

- **Skills are passed verbatim, not paraphrased.** Codex injects its installed-skill catalog into every exec session and loads the matching `SKILL.md`; configured skills use codex's `$name` / `$plugin:name` form (`DiscoverReviewSkills` in `discovery.go`). Native `codex exec review` is not used — it rejects a prompt under a scope flag and can't carry Entire's scope/per-run/checkpoint context.
- **Live tokens come from the rollout file, not stdout.** `codex exec --json` carries `usage` only on the terminal `turn.completed`, and a review is a single turn. `review_tokens.go` resolves the rollout transcript by `thread_id` (from the `thread.started` envelope), tails it (the same `~/.codex/.../rollout-*-<thread-id>.jsonl` documented under Transcript above), and emits cumulative `Tokens` per `token_count` event — the source codex's interactive UI reads.
- **No tagged review session.** Because no hook fires, codex's session is never tagged `KindAgentReview`. The fix manifest therefore sources codex from its **live run output** (`run.Buffer`), and `entire review fix` skill verification is advisory for codex (loose description match), not a hard block.

Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and (optionally) create a matching GitHub repository via the gh CLI.

Usage:
  entire enable [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, gemini, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: refs (one git ref per checkpoint; recommended) or branch (shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
  -h, --help                                 help for enable
      --import-history                       During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-github                            Initialize local git repo only; skip creating a GitHub remote
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --push                                 When bootstrapping a new repo, push the initial commit to the created GitHub remote (implies creating the remote; without it the repo is created but not pushed)
      --repo-name string                     GitHub repository name for the new repo (used when bootstrapping)
      --repo-owner string                    GitHub user or organization login for the new repo
      --repo-visibility string               GitHub repository visibility: public, private, or internal
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git, create private GitHub repo, commit, and push; then enable all agents and accept telemetry). Does not import existing agent history — see --import-history

input.content:
---
name: subagent-tracking-gaps
description: Verified state of subagent tracking in the CLI (2026-08-10) — CC transcript-path bug, no subagent data in committed checkpoints, codex now has subagent hooks, pi subagents hijack the parent session
metadata:
  type: project
---

Investigated 2026-08-10 with hook-level probes against the real binary plus upstream
sources at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/codex` and `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/pi-mono`.

**Claude Code (2.1.221) subagent transcript path is wrong.** `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd`
resolves `AgentTranscriptPath(filepath.Dir(SessionRef), agentID)` → `<slug>/agent-<id>.jsonl`,
but CC now stores it at `<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` (plus a
`agent-<id>.meta.json` carrying `agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, `spawnDepth`).
So `SubagentTranscriptPath` is always empty in production — confirmed: every real
`"subagent completed"` log line across three repos lacks the `subagent_transcript` attr,
and shadow `tasks/<id>/` holds only `checkpoint.json`, no subagent transcript. The TurnEnd
extractor (`lifecycle.go` ~line 848) uses the *correct* `<dir>/<sessionID>/subagents` path,
which masks the bug because files get picked up at Stop.

**Committed checkpoints carry zero subagent data.** Condensation (`extractSessionData`)
reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` from the shadow tree, so `tasks/<tool-use-id>/`
is dropped. 0 of 80 primary checkpoint refs in the `cli` repo contain `tasks/`; only a
legacy `v2/full` bundle does. `subagent_tokens` is null in every sampled committed
checkpoint (the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` in
`manual_commit_condensation.go` are why). `TaskStepContext` has no `TokenUsage` field at
all, and the persistent store's `IsTask`/`tasks/` write path is never invoked in production.

**Codex 0.147 DOES have subagent hooks now** — `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop` schemas in
`codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/`; stop payload includes `agent_id`, `agent_type`,
`agent_transcript_path`, `turn_id`. `hooks` and `multi_agent` are both `stable/true`.
`cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md` claiming "No subagent hooks" and "hooks require
feature flag" is stale.

**Pi subagents hijack the parent session.** Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from
the `subagent/` example extension, which spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with
`cwd` = project dir. That child auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`
and fires Entire's hooks. With `--no-session` there is no `session_file`, so pi's
`readCachedSessionID` (a single per-repo file, not per-process) returns the *parent's* ID.
Probed effect: child `session_start` errors "no session_id"; child `before_agent_start`
succeeds and overwrites the parent's `last_prompt` with the subagent's internal task text
and starts a new `turn_id`; child `agent_end` fails "transcript file not specified".

**Test coverage gaps:** the Vogon/roger-roger canary fires no subagent hooks at all
(`e2e/vogon/main.go` has no pre-task/post-task), so `TestSubagentCommitFlow` passes without
exercising the path; the real-agent version asserts nothing subagent-specific. Only
`cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/subagent_*.go` covers it, via simulated hooks against the

content.text:
## What I tested

Real-agent E2E didn't work out here, so I probed the production hook entrypoints directly (temp repos, real `entire` binary, real upstream payload shapes) and cross-checked against your own production logs and checkpoints.

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| Vogon canary `TestSubagentCommitFlow` | Passes — but **fires no subagent hooks at all**; `e2e/vogon/main.go` has no pre-task/post-task. Zero real coverage. |
| Claude Code real E2E | **Blocked locally**: `cleanConfigDir` hands the agent a blank `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so it reports "Not logged in". Only works in CI (which links `~/.claude/.claude.json`). |
| Claude Code hook-level probe | pre-task → post-task → stop → commit all fire correctly; task checkpoint lands on the shadow branch and shows as `[Task] Completed 'dev' agent: …` in `checkpoint list`. |
| Codex real E2E | You declined the run — not executed. |
| Codex hooks | No subagent verbs registered (`session-start`, `user-prompt-submit`, `stop`, `pre-tool-use`, `post-tool-use` only). |
| Pi nested-subagent probe | Parent session gets hijacked (details below). |

## Four confirmed defects

**1. Claude Code's subagent transcript is never captured.** `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` (`cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1152`) looks for `<slug>/agent-<id>.jsonl`. CC 2.1.221 actually writes `<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`. Production proof: every `"subagent completed"` line in `cli/`, `cli_experiments/` and `cli_experiments_2/` logs has `agent_id` but no `subagent_transcript` attr — it only logs when the path resolves. Consequence: task checkpoints store no subagent transcript, and file extraction silently falls back to scanning the *main* transcript, where the subagent's edits don't appear. The TurnEnd extractor at `lifecycle.go:848` uses the correct path, which is why files still get picked up at Stop — that masks it.

Bonus: upstream now also writes `agent-<id>.meta.json` with `agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, `spawnDepth` — ready-made attribution, including nesting depth, which Entire doesn't model.

**2. Committed checkpoints carry no subagent data.** `extractSessionData` reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` from the shadow tree, so `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` is dropped at condensation. **0 of 80** primary checkpoint refs in your `cli` repo contain `tasks/` (the 69 hits I found are in a legacy `v2/full` bundle). `subagent_tokens` is `null` in all 30 checkpoints I sampled — including sessions that ran dozens of subagents. The two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` in `manual_commit_condensation.go` are exactly this. `TaskStepContext` has no `TokenUsage` field, and the persistent store's `IsTask`/`tasks/` layout is never written in production.

**3. Codex has subagent hooks now and we ignore them.** `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/` defines `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop`; the stop payload carries `agent_id`, `agent_type`, **`agent_transcript_path`**, `turn_id`. Both `hooks` and `multi_agent` are `stable/true` in 0.147. `codex/AGENT.md` still says "No subagent hooks" and "hooks require feature flag" — both stale.

**4. Pi subagents corrupt the parent session.** Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from the `subagent/` example extension, which spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with `cwd` = the project. That child auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` and fires our hooks. With no session file, pi's `readCachedSessionID` — one per-repo file, not per-process — returns the *parent's* ID. Probed: child `session_start` errors `no session_id`; child `before_agent_start` **succeeds and overwrites the parent's `last_prompt`** with the subagent's internal `Task: …` text and starts a fresh `turn_id`; child `agent_end` fails `transcript file not specified`. So the checkpoint title becomes the last subagent's internal prompt and turn windows reset mid-turn.

## What needs doing

**Fix the bugs (small, high value)**
1. Resolve the CC subagent transcript at `<dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, keeping the old path as fallback. Read `meta.json` for `agentType`/`description`/`spawnDepth` instead of only parsing `tool_input`.
2. Guard pi against nested invocations (mark the child via env when spawning is detectable, or refuse a turn whose session ID came from cache with no session file) so it can't clobber the parent's prompt/turn.
3. Pass the subagents dir at the two condensation TODOs, or explicitly document why not — right now `subagent_tokens` never survives a commit.

**Decide the data model (the actual "proper tracking" question)**
4. Should subagent work be visible *after* commit? If yes: carry `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` into the committed tree (the persistent store already has the layout), enrich the task record — today it's just `session_id`/`tool_use_id`/`checkpoint_uuid`/`agent_id`, with no subagent type, description, files, tokens, or timings — and surface it (`explain`, `status`, `session tokens` already has a Subagents row it can rarely populate). If no, say so in the docs and stop building toward it.
5. Replace the cumulative-`SubagentTokens`-with-delta-rescoping-in-three-places contract with a per-subagent record; it's the fragile core of the token story.

**Codex + Pi integration**
6. Wire codex `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop` → `SubagentStart`/`SubagentEnd` (its `agent_transcript_path` makes this the cleanest integration of the three), plus a `SubagentAwareExtractor` over subagent rollouts. Refresh `AGENT.md`.
7. For pi, decide whether extension-provided subagents are in scope at all; if yes it needs a `tool_call`-based bridge in `entire_extension.ts`, since there's no native event.

**Coverage**
8. Teach Vogon to fire pre-task/post-task so the canary actually exercises the path in CI.
9. Make `TestSubagentCommitFlow` assert something subagent-specific (task checkpoint exists, subagent transcript stored, subagent tokens non-nil).
10. Add a subagent section to `docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md` — it currently says nothing, so every new agent integration skips this.

Probe repos are kept under `…/scratchpad/probe-cc`, `probe-cc2`, `probe-pi` if you want to replay any of it. Want me to run the Codex E2E (it was declined) or start on the two path bugs?

input.description: Read doc section on subagent transcripts

content.content:
Fires after a subagent finishes its work. Creates the final checkpoint for the subagent's task.

**What it does:**

1.  **Parse Input**: Extracts `tool_use_id`, `agent_id` (from `tool_response.agentId`), `session_id`, `transcript_path`, and `tool_input`.

2.  **Locate Subagent Transcript**:

    - Constructs path: `<transcript_dir>/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl`.
    - If the subagent transcript exists, uses it for file extraction; otherwise falls back to main transcript.

3.  **Extract Modified Files**: Parses the transcript (subagent or main) to find Write/Edit tool invocations.

4.  **Compute New Files**:

    - Loads pre-task state from `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.
    - Compares current untracked files against the pre-task snapshot.
    - Files that are now untracked but weren't before = files created by the subagent.

5.  **Find Checkpoint UUID**: Scans the main transcript for any checkpoint UUID associated with this `tool_use_id` (used for rewind linking).

6.  **Save Final Checkpoint**:

    - Builds `TaskCheckpointContext` with all file changes, transcript paths, subagent info, and checkpoint UUID.
    - Calls `strategy.SaveTaskCheckpoint(ctx)`.
    - Creates a commit with the subagent's file changes and metadata including the subagent transcript.

7.  **Cleanup**: Deletes `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.

### `PostToolUse[TaskCreate|TaskUpdate]`

- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code post-todo`
=== line 120-130 ===

5.  **Calculate Token Usage**:

    - Parses the transcript from `StepTranscriptStart` (captured at prompt start) to calculate tokens used in this turn.
    - Extracts token counts from assistant messages: input tokens, cache creation/read tokens, output tokens.
    - Deduplicates by message ID (streaming creates multiple rows per message; uses highest output_tokens).
    - Finds spawned subagents by scanning for `agentId:` in Task tool results.
    - Calculates subagent token usage from their transcript files (`agent-<id>.jsonl`).
    - Aggregates into a `TokenUsage` struct with nested `SubagentTokens`.

6.  **Invoke Strategy**:

    - Builds a `SaveContext` with session ID, file lists, metadata paths, git author info, and token usage.

      (they are still picked up at turn end, which is why a wrong path went unnoticed).

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(subagent): resolve subagent transcripts in Claude Code's current layout

handleLifecycleSubagentEnd looked for the subagent transcript at
<transcriptDir>/agent-<id>.jsonl, a sibling of the main transcript. Claude
Code now nests them: <transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl
(with an agent-<id>.meta.json sidecar alongside). The old path therefore never
existed, so SubagentTranscriptPath was always empty in production — confirmed
by real logs, where no "subagent completed" line ever carries the
subagent_transcript attribute (it is only logged when the path resolves).

Two consequences: task checkpoints stored no subagent transcript, and file
extraction fell back to scanning the main transcript, where a subagent's
Write/Edit calls never appear. The turn-end extractor already used the correct
nested path, so files were still picked up at Stop — which is what kept the
wrong path unnoticed.

Add ResolveAgentTranscriptPath, which prefers the nested layout and falls back
to the legacy sibling one so older sessions keep working, and route both
call sites through the new SubagentsDir helper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

git push -q -u origin soph/fix-subagent-transcript-path 2>&1 | tail -3 && gh pr create --title "fix(subagent): resolve subagent transcripts in Claude Code's current layout" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` resolved the subagent transcript as a **sibling** of the main transcript:

```
<transcriptDir>/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
```

Claude Code (verified on 2.1.221) nests them one level deeper:

```
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.meta.json   # agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth
```

So the resolved path never existed and `SubagentTranscriptPath` was always empty in production. Evidence: across three enabled repos, **every** real `"subagent completed"` log line carries `agent_id` but never the `subagent_transcript` attribute — that attribute is only appended when the path resolves.

Two consequences:

1. Task checkpoints stored **no subagent transcript** — the shadow tree's `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` held only `checkpoint.json`.
2. File extraction fell back to scanning the **main** transcript from offset 0, where a subagent's `Write`/`Edit` calls never appear.

The turn-end extractor (`lifecycle.go`) already used the correct nested path, so a subagent's files were still picked up at Stop. That masked the bug.

## Fix

- `ResolveAgentTranscriptPath(transcriptDir, sessionID, agentID)` — prefers the nested layout, falls back to the legacy sibling layout so sessions from older agent versions keep working, returns `""` when neither exists (and never resolves an empty `agentID`).
- `SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, sessionID)` — one definition of the nested directory; the turn-end extractor now uses it too instead of inlining the join.

Scoped to path resolution. The `meta.json` sidecar is documented but not yet consumed — richer subagent attribution is separate follow-up work.

## Tests

- `TestResolveAgentTranscriptPath` — nested, legacy, nested-wins-over-legacy, neither-exists, empty-agent-ID.
- `TestSubagentCheckpoints_StoresSubagentTranscript_CurrentLayout` (integration) — asserts the shadow branch contains `tasks/<tool-use-id>/agent-<id>.jsonl` and that it references the subagent's edit. **Verified RED before the fix**, green after.
- `TestSubagentCheckpoints_StoresSubagentTranscript_LegacyLayout` (integration) — regression guard for the old layout.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

1	# Entire CLI Hooks for Claude Code
2	
3	This document describes the hooks that Entire installs in Claude Code's `.claude/settings.json` to track AI-assisted development sessions.
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	Entire integrates with Claude Code through six hooks that fire at different points during a session:
8	
9	| Hook                     | Trigger                        | Purpose                                        |
10	| ------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
11	| `SessionStart`           | New chat session begins        | Generate and persist Entire session ID         |
12	| `UserPromptSubmit`       | User submits a prompt          | Capture pre-prompt state, check for conflicts  |
13	| `Stop`                   | Claude finishes responding     | Create checkpoint with code + metadata         |
14	| `PreToolUse[Agent]`      | Subagent is about to start     | Capture pre-task state for diff computation    |
15	| `PostToolUse[Agent]`     | Subagent finishes              | Create final checkpoint for subagent work      |
16	| `PostToolUse[TaskCreate\|TaskUpdate]` | Subagent updates its task list | Create incremental checkpoint if files changed |
17	
18	> **Tool matcher note.** Claude Code's subagent dispatch tool is `Agent` (there
19	> was never a `Task` tool), and the `TodoWrite` tool was disabled by default in
20	> v2.1.142 in favor of `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`. Older CLI versions installed
21	> these hooks under `Task`/`TodoWrite`, where they silently never fired. A normal
22	> `entire enable` does not rewrite existing hook config in place; re-run with
23	> `--force` (`entire enable --force`) to strip the stale entries and reinstall
24	> under the matchers above. See
25	> [tools-reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.md) and
26	> [hooks matcher rules](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md).
27	>
28	> The incremental-checkpoint handler still parses the legacy `TodoWrite`
29	> `tool_input` schema for its checkpoint message label; under `TaskCreate`/
30	> `TaskUpdate` the checkpoint is still created (file-change detection is
31	> independent) but the label falls back to `Checkpoint #N`. Richer labels from
32	> the Task* payloads are a follow-up.
33	
34	### Critical Capabilities
35	
36	  1. Prompt blocking - UserPromptSubmit hook needs to support returning a response to be shown in the cli session.
37	    - Claude Code allows us to return a JSON response to stdout that can:
38	      - Allow continuation: {"continue": true}
39	      - Block with message: {"continue": false, "stopReason": "Your message here"}
40	  2. Transcript access - Hooks receive transcript path; system needs to read it for:
41	    - Extracting user prompts
42	    - Extracting modified files
43	    - Generating summaries
44	  3. Tool use ID tracking - For subagent checkpoints, need unique tool_use_id to correlate PreToolUse and PostToolUse events
45	  4. Stdin parsing - Hook input comes as JSON on stdin; agent must define its input schema
46	
47	## Detailed Hook Info
48	
49	### `SessionStart`
50	
51	- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code session-start`
52	- **Handler**: `handleSessionStart()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:907`
53	
54	Fires when a new chat session begins in Claude Code.
55	
56	**What it does:**
57	
58	1.  **Parse Input**: Reads session details from Claude Code's hook payload (`session_id`, `session_ref`).
59	2.  **Generate Entire Session ID**: Creates a date-prefixed identifier by combining today's date with the model's session ID (e.g., `2026-01-15-ab310c99-f579-4a12-8b3c-1234567890ab`).
60	3.  **Persist Session ID**: Writes the Entire session ID to `.entire/current_session`. This file is read by subsequent hooks to maintain session context across hook invocations, even if the session spans midnight (date boundary).
61	
62	### `UserPromptSubmit`
63	
64	- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit`
65	- **Handler**: `captureInitialState()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:248`
66	
67	Fires every time the user submits a prompt. Prepares the repository state tracking _before_ Claude makes any changes.
68	
69	**What it does:**
70	
71	1.  **Concurrent Session Check**:
72	
73	    - Queries the strategy to check if another Entire session has uncommitted checkpoints on the same HEAD commit.
74	    - If a conflict is found, outputs a JSON response that blocks the prompt and shows a warning to the user.
75	    - The warning includes the other session's initial prompt (if available) and a resume command.
76	    - Sets `ConcurrentWarningShown` flag in session state so the user can continue on the next prompt.
77	    - Once the user commits their changes (or the conflict resolves), the flag is cleared automatically.
78	
79	2.  **Capture Pre-Prompt State**:
80	
81	    - Runs `git status` to get a list of all **untracked files** in the repository.
82	    - Saves this list to `.entire/tmp/pre-prompt-<session-id>.json`.
83	    - This baseline is compared later (in the `Stop` hook) to determine which files were newly created by Claude.
84	    - Records the current transcript line count (`StepTranscriptStart`) for incremental token usage calculation.
85	
86	3.  **Initialize Session Strategy**:
87	    - For strategies that implement `SessionInitializer`, calls `InitializeSession()`.
88	    - **Manual-commit strategy**: Creates or validates the shadow branch (`entire/<HEAD-hash[:7]>`), saves session state to `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json` with `BaseCommit`, `WorktreePath`, and `AgentType`.
89	    - Handles shadow branch conflicts (from other worktrees) and session ID conflicts with appropriate error messages and recovery options.
90	
91	### `Stop`
92	
93	- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code stop`
94	- **Handler**: `commitWithMetadata()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:288`
95	
96	Fires when Claude finishes responding. Does **not** fire on user interrupt (Ctrl+C).
97	
98	**What it does:**
99	
100	1.  **Parse Transcript**:
101	
102	    - Reads the JSONL transcript from the path provided by Claude Code.
103	    - Parses the full transcript. `CheckpointTranscriptStart` (or `StepTranscriptStart` from pre-prompt state) is used to detect whether new content exists since the last checkpoint.
104	    - Extracts **modified files** by scanning for Write/Edit tool uses in the transcript.
105	
106	2.  **Extract and Save Metadata** (to `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/`):
107	
108	    - `full.jsonl` - Copy of the complete transcript.
109	    - `prompt.txt` - Checkpoint-scoped user prompts, separated by `---`.
110	    - `summary.txt` - The last assistant message (used as checkpoint summary).
111	
112	3.  **Compute File Changes**:
113	
114	    - **Modified files**: Extracted from transcript (Write/Edit tool invocations).
115	    - **New files**: Compare current untracked files against pre-prompt state to find files created by Claude.
116	    - **Deleted files**: Query `git status` for tracked files that no longer exist.
117	    - All paths are normalized relative to repo root (not cwd) to handle Claude running from subdirectories.
118	
119	4.  **Generate Commit Message**: Derives from the last user prompt, truncated and formatted appropriately.
120	
121	5.  **Calculate Token Usage**:
122	
123	    - Parses the transcript from `StepTranscriptStart` (captured at prompt start) to calculate tokens used in this turn.
124	    - Extracts token counts from assistant messages: input tokens, cache creation/read tokens, output tokens.
125	    - Deduplicates by message ID (streaming creates multiple rows per message; uses highest output_tokens).
126	    - Finds spawned subagents by scanning for `agentId:` in Task tool results.
127	    - Calculates subagent token usage from their transcript files (`agent-<id>.jsonl`).
128	    - Aggregates into a `TokenUsage` struct with nested `SubagentTokens`.
129	
130	6.  **Invoke Strategy**:
131	
132	    - Builds a `SaveContext` with session ID, file lists, metadata paths, git author info, and token usage.
133	    - Calls `strategy.SaveChanges(ctx)` to create the checkpoint.

content.content:
### Plugin File Pattern (Pi)

Pi uses a TypeScript extension file (`.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`) instead of a JSON config. The extension is embedded in the Go binary via `//go:embed` and installed by `entire enable --agent pi`.

Pi extension hooks fire via `execFile` (non-blocking) to avoid blocking the agent. The extension listens for Pi lifecycle events (`session_start`, `before_agent_start`, `agent_end`, `session_shutdown`) and dispatches each to `entire hooks pi <event>` with a JSON payload containing `type`, `cwd`, `session_file`, `session_id`, and (for `before_agent_start`) `prompt`.

Key differences from JSON config agents:
- Extension file is written/removed entirely (not partial JSON edits)
- Uses `node:child_process.execFile` for all hook invocations
- Session ID is cached to `.entire/tmp/pi/pi-active-session` to bridge races between `session_start` and `before_agent_start`/`agent_end`
- On `agent_end`, the Pi JSONL transcript is captured to `.entire/tmp/pi/<id>.json` for stable reference even if native Pi sessions are deleted
- `session_shutdown` is cleanup-only (no `SessionEnd` event) to avoid a race with `agent_end`'s checkpoint save
- Idempotency via marker string check: `"Auto-generated by \`entire enable --agent pi\`"`

See `cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/entire_extension.ts` for the full extension source.

### Plugin File Pattern (OpenCode)

OpenCode uses a TypeScript plugin file (`.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`) instead of a JSON config. The plugin is auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode` and uses OpenCode's Bun-based plugin API.

git push -q -u origin soph/fix-pi-nested-subagent-session 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --title "fix(pi): stop nested subagent processes from claiming the parent session" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Pi has no subagent lifecycle events. Subagents come from an extension — see Pi's `subagent/` example — which spawns one nested process per task:

```
pi --mode json -p --no-session      # cwd = the project directory
```

Pi auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/*/index.ts` from that cwd, so **the child loads Entire's own extension** and forwards its lifecycle as if it were the user's session. Because it runs with `--no-session` it reports no session file, so the payload carries no resolvable session ID — and the session-ID cache is a single per-repo file, so the unconditional fallback handed the child its **parent's** ID.

Probed against the real hook entrypoints:

| Child hook | Before |
| --- | --- |
| `session_start` | errors `no session_id in SessionStart event` |
| `before_agent_start` | **succeeds** — overwrites the parent's `last_prompt` with the subagent's internal `Task: …` text and opens a new `turn_id` mid-flight |
| `agent_end` | fails `transcript file not specified` |

So the checkpoint's title and its turn-scoped transcript/token windows described the subagent instead of the user's request.

## Fix

Two guards, so neither has to be perfect:

1. **Extension** — returns early when `process.env.ENTIRE_PI_NESTED` is already set, and sets it otherwise so any Pi this process spawns is marked nested. The marker is read **only** by the extension: Entire's own hook subprocesses inherit it, so the CLI side must never treat it as a skip signal.
2. **CLI** (`nestedInvocation`) — refuses to resolve a payload with no session file against the cache. This also covers third-party subagent extensions and Pi builds that predate the marker.

Preserved:

- The legitimate cache fallback — session file present, but its name carries no parseable ID.
- An explicit payload `session_id`; only the *cache* is distrusted.
- `agent_end` loses nothing: `captureTranscript` returns `""` without a session file, so such an event could only ever fail downstream with "transcript file not specified". The guard turns that error into a clean skip.

## Tests

- `TestParseHookEvent_NestedInvocation_DoesNotClaimParentSession` — a populated parent cache, then the three child payloads with no session file: no event emitted, parent's cache untouched. **Verified RED** (`nested before_agent_start emitted TurnStart for session "parent-id"`).
- `TestParseHookEvent_CacheFallbackStillAppliesWithSessionFile` — regression guard for the legitimate fallback.
- `TestParseHookEvent_ExplicitSessionIDNeedsNoSessionFile` — explicit IDs still honoured.
- `TestInstallHooks` now asserts the installed extension carries the nesting guard.

Also verified end to end against the real binary: after the nested lifecycle, the parent session's `last_prompt` and `turn_id` are unchanged and no second session appears.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

1	# Agent Implementation Guide
2	
3	Before implementing, read the [Agent Integration Checklist](agent-integration-checklist.md) for design principles (full transcript storage, native format preservation) and validation criteria.
4	
5	## Architecture Overview
6	
7	The Entire CLI uses **inversion of control** for agent integration: agents are passive data providers that translate their native hook payloads into normalized lifecycle events, and the framework handles all orchestration (state transitions, file detection, checkpoint saving, metadata generation). The flow is:
8	
9	```
10	Agent hook invocation → ParseHookEvent() → Event → DispatchLifecycleEvent() → framework actions
11	```
12	
13	An agent never calls strategy methods or manages session state directly. It only answers questions: "What event just happened?" and "What does the transcript say?"
14	
15	## Quick Reference
16	
17	### Core Interface (`Agent`)
18	
19	Every agent must implement all 19 methods on the `Agent` interface:
20	
21	| Group | Method | Purpose |
22	|-------|--------|---------|
23	| **Identity** | `Name()` | Registry key (e.g., `"claude-code"`) |
24	| | `Type()` | Display name for metadata (e.g., `"Claude Code"`) |
25	| | `Description()` | Human-readable description for UI |
26	| | `DetectPresence()` | Check if agent is configured in the repo |
27	| | `ProtectedDirs()` | Directories to preserve during rewind |
28	| **Event Mapping** | `HookNames()` | Hook verbs that become CLI subcommands |
29	| | `ParseHookEvent()` | **Core contribution surface** - translate native hooks to Events |
30	| **Transcript** | `ReadTranscript()` | Read raw transcript bytes |
31	| | `ChunkTranscript()` | Split large transcripts at format-aware boundaries |
32	| | `ReassembleTranscript()` | Recombine chunks into a single transcript |
33	| **Session Management** | `GetHookConfigPath()` | Path to hook config file |
34	| | `SupportsHooks()` | Whether agent supports lifecycle hooks |
35	| | `ParseHookInput()` | Parse hook callback input from stdin |
36	| | `GetSessionID()` | Extract session ID from hook input |
37	| | `GetSessionDir()` | Where agent stores session data |
38	| | `ResolveSessionFile()` | Path to session transcript file |
39	| | `ReadSession()` | Read session data from agent's storage |
40	| | `WriteSession()` | Write session data for resumption |
41	| | `FormatResumeCommand()` | Command to resume a session |
42	
43	### Optional Interfaces
44	
45	| Interface | Methods | When to implement |
46	|-----------|---------|-------------------|
47	| `HookSupport` | `InstallHooks`, `UninstallHooks`, `AreHooksInstalled`, `GetSupportedHooks` | Agent uses a config file for hook registration (e.g., `settings.json`) |
48	| `HookHandler` | `GetHookNames` | **Required for CLI hook registration** — `entire hooks <agent> <verb>` subcommands are only created for agents implementing this interface. Typically delegates to `HookNames()`. |
49	| `TranscriptAnalyzer` | `GetTranscriptPosition`, `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` | You want richer checkpoints with transcript-derived file lists |
50	| `TranscriptPreparer` | `PrepareTranscript` | Agent writes transcripts asynchronously and needs a flush/sync step |
51	| `TokenCalculator` | `CalculateTokenUsage` | Agent's transcript contains token usage data |
52	| `SubagentAwareExtractor` | `ExtractAllModifiedFiles`, `CalculateTotalTokenUsage` | Agent spawns subagents (like Claude Code's Task tool) |
53	| `HookResponseWriter` | `WriteHookResponse` | Agent can display messages from hook responses (e.g., session start banner). Claude Code uses JSON `systemMessage` on stdout; Factory AI Droid uses plain text on stdout. |
54	| `ContextInjector` | `InjectionEvent`, `RenderContextInjection` | Agent can inject text into the **model's** context window (distinct from `HookResponseWriter`, which targets the *user*). The agent declares which lifecycle event it injects at and renders a native stdout payload. The dispatcher (`emitContextInjection`) emits it once per normal session via `session.State.ContextInjectionDecided`, skipping review/investigate sessions, and only when fresh clone-local preferences say trails are enabled for the current repo/API/auth target. The API check happens before the prompt path (`entire enable`, successful `entire trail ...` commands, and stale/missing cache refresh on SessionStart all refresh `ClonePreferences.TrailsEnabled` using `api.Client.TrailsEnabled`); TurnStart performs no auth/network work and leaves unknown/stale caches undecided so a later refresh can still inject. Claude Code / Codex / Gemini inject at `TurnStart` using `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (UserPromptSubmit / BeforeAgent); Pi and OpenCode emit a `{"inject_context":...}` envelope that their embedded extension applies (Pi via a `before_agent_start` message, OpenCode via `experimental.chat.system.transform`). |
55	| `FileWatcher` | `GetWatchPaths`, `OnFileChange` | Agent doesn't support hooks; uses file-based detection instead |
56	
57	## Step-by-Step Implementation Guide
58	
59	### Step 1: Create Package
60	
61	Create a new directory under `cmd/entire/cli/agent/`:
62	
63	```
64	cmd/entire/cli/agent/youragent/
65	├── youragent.go          # Core Agent implementation + init()
66	├── lifecycle.go          # ParseHookEvent + compile-time assertions
67	├── types.go              # Hook input structs, transcript types, tool constants
68	├── hooks.go              # HookSupport implementation (if applicable)
69	├── transcript.go         # TranscriptAnalyzer implementation (if applicable)
70	├── lifecycle_test.go     # Tests for ParseHookEvent
71	├── hooks_test.go         # Tests for hook installation
72	└── transcript_test.go    # Tests for transcript analysis
73	```
74	
75	### Step 2: Define Types (`types.go`)

79	```go

package strategy

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/id"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// TestCondenseSession_CommittedCheckpointCarriesSubagentTokens pins the
// checkpoint-scoped subagent total onto the committed checkpoint's metadata.
//
// Condensation recomputes token usage from the transcript with subagentsDir="",
// which by contract leaves SubagentTokens nil, and that recomputed value overwrote
// the checkpoint-scoped total SaveStep had already rescoped into
// state.CheckpointTokenUsage. Result: committed checkpoints reported
// "subagent_tokens": null even for sessions that ran many subagents (0 of 30
// sampled real checkpoints carried one).
func TestCondenseSession_CommittedCheckpointCarriesSubagentTokens(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	ctx := context.Background()
	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "2026-08-10-condense-subagent-tokens"

	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))

	// The assistant line carries real usage, so the transcript recompute fires and
	// produces main-agent tokens with no SubagentTokens — the overwrite this test
	// guards against.
	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"delegate to a subagent"}}
{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a1","message":{"id":"m1","usage":{"input_tokens":300,"output_tokens":150}}}
`
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName), []byte(transcript), 0o644))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt"), []byte("agent-modified"), 0o644))

	require.NoError(t, s.SaveStep(ctx, StepContext{
		SessionID:      sessionID,
		MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
		MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
		ModifiedFiles:  []string{"test.txt"},
		CommitMessage:  "checkpoint 1",
		AuthorName:     "Test",
		AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
		AgentType:      agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		TokenUsage: &agent.TokenUsage{
			InputTokens: 100, OutputTokens: 50, APICallCount: 1,
			SubagentTokens: &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 500, OutputTokens: 250, APICallCount: 5},
		},
	}))

	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens,
		"precondition: SaveStep records the checkpoint-scoped subagent total")

	checkpointID := id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd3344")
	result, err := s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, checkpointID, state, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.False(t, result.Skipped, "condensation must not skip when files are touched")

	summary := readCheckpointSummary(t, repo, checkpointID)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage, "committed checkpoint must carry token usage")
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens,
		"committed checkpoint must carry the checkpoint-scoped subagent total")
	require.Equal(t, 500, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 250, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 5, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.APICallCount)

	// The session-wide cumulative must be untouched by the fill, so
	// resetCheckpointWindow still snapshots the right baseline for the next window.
	stateAfter, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, stateAfter.SubagentTokensBaseline,
		"condensation must still snapshot the cumulative subagent baseline")
	require.Equal(t, 500, stateAfter.SubagentTokensBaseline.InputTokens)
}

// TestCondenseSession_SubagentTokensStayScopedToCheckpointWindow covers the second
// checkpoint of a session: the committed value must be that window's delta, not the
// session-wide cumulative, so summing checkpoints does not over-count.
func TestCondenseSession_SubagentTokensStayScopedToCheckpointWindow(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	ctx := context.Background()
	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "2026-08-10-condense-subagent-window"

	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))
	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"delegate again"}}
{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a1","message":{"id":"m1","usage":{"input_tokens":300,"output_tokens":150}}}
`
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName), []byte(transcript), 0o644))

	saveStep := func(commitMsg, content string, subagent *agent.TokenUsage) {
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt"), []byte(content), 0o644))
		require.NoError(t, s.SaveStep(ctx, StepContext{
			SessionID:      sessionID,
			MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
			MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
			ModifiedFiles:  []string{"test.txt"},
			CommitMessage:  commitMsg,
			AuthorName:     "Test",
			AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
			AgentType:      agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
			TokenUsage: &agent.TokenUsage{
				InputTokens: 100, OutputTokens: 50, APICallCount: 1,
				SubagentTokens: subagent,
			},
		}))
	}

	// Checkpoint 1: subagent cumulative 500/250.
	saveStep("checkpoint 1", "v2", &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 500, OutputTokens: 250, APICallCount: 5})
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd5566"), state, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Checkpoint 2: the subagent grew to 620/310 cumulative — a 120/60 delta.
	saveStep("checkpoint 2", "v3", &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 620, OutputTokens: 310, APICallCount: 6})
	state2, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	secondID := id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd7788")
	_, err = s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, secondID, state2, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	summary := readCheckpointSummary(t, repo, secondID)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 120, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens,
		"second checkpoint must carry its window's delta, not the session cumulative")
	require.Equal(t, 60, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)
}

// readCheckpointSummary reads a committed checkpoint's root CheckpointSummary off
// the metadata branch.
func readCheckpointSummary(t *testing.T, repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) checkpoint.CheckpointSummary {
	t.Helper()

	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	checkpointTree, err := tree.Tree(checkpointID.Path())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rootMeta, err := checkpointTree.File(paths.MetadataFileName)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rootBytes, err := rootMeta.Contents()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var summary checkpoint.CheckpointSummary
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(rootBytes), &summary))
	return summary
}

package strategy

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// TestCondenseSession_CommittedCheckpointCarriesSubagentTokens pins the
// checkpoint-scoped subagent total onto the committed checkpoint's metadata.
//
// Condensation recomputes token usage from the transcript with subagentsDir="",
// which by contract leaves SubagentTokens nil, and that recomputed value overwrote
// the checkpoint-scoped total SaveStep had already rescoped into
// state.CheckpointTokenUsage. Result: committed checkpoints reported
// "subagent_tokens": null even for sessions that ran many subagents (0 of 30
// sampled real checkpoints carried one).
func TestCondenseSession_CommittedCheckpointCarriesSubagentTokens(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	ctx := context.Background()
	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "2026-08-10-condense-subagent-tokens"

	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))

	// The assistant line carries real usage, so the transcript recompute fires and
	// produces main-agent tokens with no SubagentTokens — the overwrite this test
	// guards against.
	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"delegate to a subagent"}}
{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a1","message":{"id":"m1","usage":{"input_tokens":300,"output_tokens":150}}}
`
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName), []byte(transcript), 0o644))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt"), []byte("agent-modified"), 0o644))

	require.NoError(t, s.SaveStep(ctx, StepContext{
		SessionID:      sessionID,
		MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
		MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
		ModifiedFiles:  []string{"test.txt"},
		CommitMessage:  "checkpoint 1",
		AuthorName:     "Test",
		AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
		AgentType:      agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		TokenUsage: &agent.TokenUsage{
			InputTokens: 100, OutputTokens: 50, APICallCount: 1,
			SubagentTokens: &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 500, OutputTokens: 250, APICallCount: 5},
		},
	}))

	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens,
		"precondition: SaveStep records the checkpoint-scoped subagent total")

	checkpointID := id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd3344")
	result, err := s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, checkpointID, state, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.False(t, result.Skipped, "condensation must not skip when files are touched")

	summary := readCheckpointSummary(t, repo, checkpointID)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage, "committed checkpoint must carry token usage")
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens,
		"committed checkpoint must carry the checkpoint-scoped subagent total")
	require.Equal(t, 500, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 250, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 5, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.APICallCount)

	// The session-wide cumulative must be untouched by the fill, so
	// resetCheckpointWindow still snapshots the right baseline for the next window.
	stateAfter, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, stateAfter.SubagentTokensBaseline,
		"condensation must still snapshot the cumulative subagent baseline")
	require.Equal(t, 500, stateAfter.SubagentTokensBaseline.InputTokens)
}

// TestCondenseSession_SubagentTokensStayScopedToCheckpointWindow covers the second
// checkpoint of a session: the committed value must be that window's delta, not the
// session-wide cumulative, so summing checkpoints does not over-count.
func TestCondenseSession_SubagentTokensStayScopedToCheckpointWindow(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	ctx := context.Background()
	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "2026-08-10-condense-subagent-window"

	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))
	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"delegate again"}}
{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a1","message":{"id":"m1","usage":{"input_tokens":300,"output_tokens":150}}}
`
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName), []byte(transcript), 0o644))

	saveStep := func(commitMsg, content string, subagent *agent.TokenUsage) {
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt"), []byte(content), 0o644))
		require.NoError(t, s.SaveStep(ctx, StepContext{
			SessionID:      sessionID,
			MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
			MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
			ModifiedFiles:  []string{"test.txt"},
			CommitMessage:  commitMsg,
			AuthorName:     "Test",
			AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
			AgentType:      agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
			TokenUsage: &agent.TokenUsage{
				InputTokens: 100, OutputTokens: 50, APICallCount: 1,
				SubagentTokens: subagent,
			},
		}))
	}

	// Checkpoint 1: subagent cumulative 500/250.
	saveStep("checkpoint 1", "v2", &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 500, OutputTokens: 250, APICallCount: 5})
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd5566"), state, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Checkpoint 2: the subagent grew to 620/310 cumulative — a 120/60 delta.
	saveStep("checkpoint 2", "v3", &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 620, OutputTokens: 310, APICallCount: 6})
	state2, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	secondID := id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd7788")
	_, err = s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, secondID, state2, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	summary := readCheckpointSummary(t, repo, secondID)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 120, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens,
		"second checkpoint must carry its window's delta, not the session cumulative")
	require.Equal(t, 60, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)
}

// readCheckpointSummary reads a committed checkpoint's root CheckpointSummary off
// the metadata branch.
func readCheckpointSummary(t *testing.T, repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) checkpoint.CheckpointSummary {
	t.Helper()

	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	checkpointTree, err := tree.Tree(checkpointID.Path())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rootMeta, err := checkpointTree.File(paths.MetadataFileName)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rootBytes, err := rootMeta.Contents()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var summary checkpoint.CheckpointSummary
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(rootBytes), &summary))
	return summary
}

git push -q -u origin soph/fix-condensation-subagent-tokens 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --title "fix(checkpoint): carry subagent tokens through to committed checkpoints" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Committed checkpoints reported `"subagent_tokens": null` even for sessions that ran many subagents — **0 of 30** sampled real checkpoints in this repo carried one, despite logs showing dozens of subagent completions in those same sessions. Two independent drops:

**1. Condensation.** `extractSessionData` recomputes token usage from the transcript with `subagentsDir=""`, which by contract leaves `SubagentTokens` nil, and that recomputed value replaced what `SaveStep` produced. The session-wide cumulative survived on `state.TokenUsage` (so `entire status` still showed subagent usage), but the value written to checkpoint metadata lost it. This is what the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` markers were pointing at.

**2. The store's aggregation.** `aggregateTokenUsage`, which sums a checkpoint's sessions into the root `metadata.json`, copied only the five scalar fields. So even once per-session metadata carried `SubagentTokens`, the root total was still null. (The `cli` package's own `addCheckpointTokenUsage` already recursed — this one never did.)

## Fix

**Condensation** — fill from `state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens` rather than re-reading subagent transcripts:

- `SaveStep` already rescoped that value to this window (cumulative minus `SubagentTokensBaseline`), so checkpoints stay summable instead of each re-reporting the session total.
- A re-read would return a cumulative snapshot needing the same rescoping, and finds nothing once the agent has cleaned the transcripts up.
- The fill **copies rather than mutates**: `state.TokenUsage` can alias that struct after `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` adopts it (Copilot CLI), and mutating would overwrite the session cumulative with a window delta, making `resetCheckpointWindow` snapshot a too-small baseline for the next window.
- It runs **after** `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage`, which must see the recomputed usage without the fill.

**Store** — recurse into `SubagentTokens`. Summing is correct at that level: it aggregates across the *sessions* of one checkpoint and each session's value is already checkpoint-scoped. The replace-don't-add rule applies to accumulating steps *within* a session, where each step re-reports a cumulative snapshot.

Both `//TODO` markers are replaced with the actual reason the recompute passes `""`.

**Known gap, now documented in code + CLAUDE.md:** a mid-turn commit that condenses before any `SaveStep` in the window has no `CheckpointTokenUsage` to draw on and still records no subagent tokens.

## Tests

All three **verified RED** before the fix:

- `TestCondenseSession_CommittedCheckpointCarriesSubagentTokens` — drives a real `SaveStep` → `CondenseSession`, reads the root `CheckpointSummary` off the metadata branch, and asserts the subagent total is there; also asserts the session-wide cumulative survives untouched (the aliasing guard).
- `TestCondenseSession_SubagentTokensStayScopedToCheckpointWindow` — second checkpoint of a session (through the real `CondenseSessionByID` reset path) must carry its window's 120/60 delta, not the 620/310 cumulative, so summing checkpoints does not over-count.
- `TestAggregateTokenUsage_SumsSubagentTokens` — store-level: single session, two sessions summed, one-sided, no-subagents-stays-nil, both-nil.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

The branch's tracking config (`branch.<name>.pushRemote`, `remote.pushDefault`, `branch.<name>.remote`) is deliberately **not** a tier: election is compared against the remote of the push being made, so electing the tracking remote silently drops checkpoint sync on every push to a different remote (`git push <other> HEAD`, a `git clone -o base` pushing checkpoints to a separately added `origin`, any repo with `remote.pushDefault`), and elects a remote the read paths — which resolve through origin's remote-tracking refs — cannot see. For a fork setup where `origin` is an unpushable base repo, name the fork with `checkpoint_push_remote`. Pushes to any other remote or to a raw URL never carry checkpoint data; the dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL mode is exempt. `entire status` shows the sync destination and an unpushed-checkpoint count.
685	- **OPF (OpenAI Privacy Filter) runs at pre-push, not post-commit**: when `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.enabled` is true, the PrePush hook re-redacts unpushed `entire/checkpoints/v1` commits with the OPF 9th layer, builds new commits carrying an `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` trailer, and atomically updates the local v1 ref before pushing. Per-commit condensation stays on the fast 8-layer pipeline. See `strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go` and `docs/security-and-privacy.md` for the full flow, including divergence detection, bootstrap caps, and CAS-on-conflict semantics.
686	- Safe to use on main/master since it never modifies commit history
